findings.observed: When a helper remains alive after the initial bounded joins, close_and_join forcibly closes process.stderr but records no forced-close state. _stderr treats any subsequent empty read as natural EOF. Thus a reader unblocked by that forced close can set stderr_eof, stop, and allow stderr_log_complete true with no cleanup_error.
findings.expected: A stderr stream force-closed to unblock teardown must be classified as incomplete regardless of how the stream API presents the closure; only natural post-reap EOF may support stderr_log_complete.
findings.reproduction: Use a stderr reader blocked before consuming a remaining buffered suffix until close_and_join reaches its forced stream-close branch. The branch closes stderr; a realistic stream may then return b'' rather than raise. _stderr sets stderr_eof at controller.py:232-233, the second join observes no live helper, and controller.py:194-197 can mark the prefix log complete even though the closure—not proved natural EOF—ended reading.
findings.impact: The final cleanup artifact can once again certify a truncated MCP stderr log as complete in the exact forced-closure timeout path the repair was required to fail closed.
findings.no_fix_consequence: C3/C4 may accept misleading diagnostics and successful completion after a bounded teardown cut off unread stderr bytes, defeating the retained server-log evidence boundary.
findings.smallest_fix: Record an explicit stderr-forced-close flag before closing process.stderr in the fallback branch and require that flag to be false for stderr_log_complete; otherwise retain an incomplete-log error and cleanup_error. Add this state to the already planned coordinated regression rather than adding a separate framework.
findings.complexity: Low and confined to the existing transport teardown state.
findings.regression_risk: Low: only forced stderr closure becomes conservatively fail-closed; natural EOF, stdout framing, cancellation, exact reap, and unrelated routes remain unchanged.
findings.verification_cost: Low: extend the planned deterministic coordinated transport regression with a stream that returns EOF after forced close; no MCP process or hardware is required.
findings.alternatives: Treating empty read as sufficient cannot distinguish natural EOF from controller-forced closure. Waiting unboundedly would violate the existing cleanup deadline.
findings.cost_benefit: The demonstrated false-complete cleanup record outweighs the localized flag/check and its focused verification cost.
